cases.description: Microsoft's documented worked example: right-tailed chi-squared probability at x=18.307 with 10 degrees of freedom
cases.expected_note: Microsoft's page publishes this example's result as 0.0500006. Independently derived from the documented right-tail definition P(X > x): scipy.stats.chi2.sf(18.307, 10) = 0.05000058909139812 -> 0.0500006 at 7 dp

cases.description: A second point on the distribution, at 1 degree of freedom
cases.expected_note: Derived from the same documented right-tail definition: scipy.stats.chi2.sf(3, 1) = 0.08326451666355042 -> 0.0832645 at 7 dp. Equivalently 2*(1 - Phi(sqrt(3)))

cases.description: A non-integer degrees-of-freedom argument, which the documentation says is truncated
cases.expected_note: Excel documents "If deg_freedom is not an integer, it is truncated", so 10.9 must behave exactly as 10 and return the documented 0.0500006. Independently checked that this discriminates: a genuine 10.9 degrees of freedom would give chi2.sf(18.307, 10.9) = 0.0719365
Excel documents: "If deg_freedom < 1 or deg_freedom > 10^10, CHISQ.DIST.RT returns the #NUM! error value."
Excel documents: "If either argument is nonnumeric, CHISQ.DIST.RT function returns the #VALUE! error value."
